docs.title: RNAZoo
docs.text: A Nextflow pipeline that runs 23 RNA deep learning models, each from its own container image.

docs.title: What's included
docs.text:
The 23 models fall into six tracks: 13 task programs and 10 embedding models (the nine foundation models and SpliceBERT). The model overview lists each model's task, input, output, GPU needs and license.

Track Models Translation RiboNN, Riboformer, RiboTIE, TranslationAI, Saluki, CodonTransformer RNA foundation models RNA-FM, RiNALMo, ERNIE-RNA, Orthrus, HydraRNA, RNAErnie, PlantRNA-FM, CaLM, mRNABERT RNA structure RhoFold, SPOT-RNA, DRfold2 RNA modification MultiRM Splicing Pangolin, SpliceAI, SpliceBERT mRNA design UTR-LM

Each embedding model writes one vector per sequence (sequence_embeddings.npy, with the sequence names in labels.txt) and, with --<model>_per_token, one per token. All but SpliceBERT can train a prediction head on your labels (Fine Tuning).

docs.title: How it runs
docs.text:
• Each model has its own image, ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-<name>, with the weights inside, so nothing is downloaded at run time. Most models have a GPU image and a smaller CPU image.
  • A model runs only when its input parameter is set, so one command can run one model or several in parallel.
  • Docker or Singularity runs the images. Add gpu or cpu to the profile. Orthrus, HydraRNA and DRfold2 need a GPU and are skipped under cpu.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
From the cloned repository, with Nextflow and Docker installed (Installation):

# Test run: 19 models on the test inputs in tests/data/
nextflow run main.nf -profile test,docker,cpu

# One model on your own FASTA
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --rnafm_input my_sequences.fa

On a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, write gpu instead of cpu. The Quick Start shows more options, and Direct Docker usage runs the images without Nextflow.

docs.title: License
docs.text: The RNA-Zoo pipeline code is released under the MIT License. Each model keeps its own terms for its code, weights and container image, listed in the model overview and on its page: some forbid commercial use, and for some the weights carry no license statement, which leaves their use unclear. Please cite RNA-Zoo (CITATION.cff) and the paper of every model you run.

docs.title: Run containers directly (no Nextflow)
docs.text: Each image holds a model, its weights and a command-line entry point, so a single docker run is enough for a quick test or a bug report. For larger runs, Nextflow adds parallel tasks, resuming and file staging; see the Quick Start.

docs.title: Common recipe
docs.text:
mkdir -p /path/to/output    # otherwise Docker creates it, owned by root
docker run --rm \
    -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
    -v /path/to/output:/out \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-rnafm-cpu:latest \
    rnafm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For another model, change the image and the command (table below). For a GPU, drop -cpu from the image name and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all, or --gpus all; both need the NVIDIA Container Toolkit.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• User. -u $(id -u):$(id -g) makes the output files yours instead of root's. It needs -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) too: PyTorch can fail at import when your user ID has no entry in the container's /etc/passwd.
  • Threads. The pipeline caps each task's threads at --task_cpus with environment variables such as OMP_NUM_THREADS (the full list is in nextflow.config). A bare docker run sets none, so PyTorch, TensorFlow and BLAS may start a thread per core; add, for example, -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 on a shared machine.
  • Log output. If the log appears only at the end when piped or redirected, add -e PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1.

docs.title: Per-model commands
docs.text:
These commands use the mounts of the common recipe. Image names leave out the prefix ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo- and the tag :latest. The embedding models also take --per-token.

Model CPU image GPU image Command RNA-FM rnafm-cpu rnafm rnafm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out RiNALMo rinalmo-cpu rinalmo rinalmo_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out ERNIE-RNA ernierna ernierna ernierna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out Orthrus none orthrus orthrus_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out HydraRNA none hydrarna hydrarna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out RNAErnie rnaernie-cpu rnaernie rnaernie_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out PlantRNA-FM plantrnafm-cpu plantrnafm plantrnafm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out CaLM calm-cpu calm calm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out mRNABERT mrnabert-cpu mrnabert mrnabert_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out SpliceBERT splicebert-cpu splicebert splicebert_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out RhoFold rhofold-cpu rhofold rhofold_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out SPOT-RNA spotrna-cpu spotrna spotrna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out --cpu 4; on the GPU image, --gpu 0 instead of --cpu 4 DRfold2 none drfold2 drfold2_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out MultiRM multirm-cpu multirm multirm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out UTR-LM utrlm-cpu utrlm utrlm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out --task mrl --model-dir /opt/utrlm/Model CodonTransformer codontransformer-cpu codontransformer codon_transformer_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out/optimized_codons.fa --organism "Homo sapiens" Saluki saluki-cpu saluki saluki_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out; to set the splice track, mount an exon-length TSV and add --exons /data/exons.tsv TranslationAI translationai-cpu none (the tool hides the GPU) bash -c "cp /data/input.fa /tmp/input.fa && translationai -I /tmp/input.fa -t 0.5,0.5 && cp /tmp/input_pred*.txt /out/"

Orthrus, HydraRNA and DRfold2 have no CPU image; run them with the GPU options.

docs.title: Models with other inputs
docs.text:
RiboNN reads a TSV and must run from /app:

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    -v /path/to/input.tsv:/data/input.tsv \
    -v /path/to/output:/out \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-ribonn-cpu:latest \
    bash -c "cd /app && python3 /opt/bin/ribonn_predict.py -i /data/input.tsv -o /out --species human"

SpliceAI and Pangolin read several files. Put them in one directory, mounted as /work:

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    -v /path/to/inputs:/work \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-spliceai-cpu:latest \
    spliceai_predict.py -i /work/variants.vcf -o /work/variants.spliceai.vcf \
        -r /work/genome.fa -a grch38

For Pangolin, use the image rnazoo-pangolin-cpu and the command pangolin_predict.py -i /work/variants.vcf -r /work/genome.fa -a /work/annotation.db -o /work/variants.pangolin. Its page shows how to build annotation.db from a GTF.

RiboTIE runs in a directory that holds config.yml and the input files (config layout). On the GPU image rnazoo-tristan, pass --accelerator gpu.

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    -v "$PWD":/work -w /work \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-tristan-cpu:latest \
    bash -c "mkdir -p ribotie_out/dbs ribotie_out/out && ribotie config.yml --accelerator cpu --overwrite_data"

Riboformer reads a dataset directory mounted under /opt/Riboformer/datasets/ and writes its outputs, model_prediction.txt among them, into that directory. With a copy of the test data from the repository:

cp -r tests/data/riboformer my_data
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    -v "$PWD/my_data":/opt/Riboformer/datasets/my_data \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-riboformer-cpu:latest \
    bash -c "python data_processing.py -d my_data -r GSM3358138_filter_Cm_ctrl -t GSM3358140_freeze_Mg_ctrl && python transfer.py -i my_data -m bacteria_cm_mg"

docs.title: Help and debugging
docs.text:
Each RNA-Zoo wrapper lists its options with --help:

docker run --rm ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-rnafm-cpu:latest rnafm_predict.py --help

To look around inside an image, start a shell:

docker run --rm -it -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
    ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-rnafm-cpu:latest bash

The wrappers are in /opt/bin (ERNIE-RNA's in /opt/ernie-rna). Most upstream code is under /opt; RiboNN's is under /app.

docs.title: Fine Tuning
docs.text: The nine RNA foundation models can train a small prediction head on your labeled sequences. The model itself stays frozen: its embeddings feed a linear, MLP or XGBoost head, for regression or classification. SpliceBERT, the tenth embedding model, has no fine-tuning parameters. RiboNN, UTR-LM and RiboTIE fine-tune in their own ways; see Other fine-tuning.

docs.title: Supported models
docs.text:
Each model's parameters start with its prefix, for example --rnafm_finetune_input.

Model Prefix Embedding width Embed and train in one run (Path A) RNA-FM rnafm 640 CPU or GPU RiNALMo rinalmo 1280 CPU or GPU ERNIE-RNA ernierna 768 CPU or GPU Orthrus orthrus 512 GPU only; always embeds with large-4track HydraRNA hydrarna 1024 GPU only RNAErnie rnaernie 768 CPU or GPU PlantRNA-FM plantrnafm 480 CPU or GPU CaLM calm 768 CPU or GPU mRNABERT mrnabert 768 CPU or GPU

Training on saved embeddings (Path B) runs on the CPU for every model and accepts any width, for example 256 from an Orthrus base-4track run.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --rnafm_finetune_input my_labels.tsv \
  --rnafm_finetune_label te

Results go to results/rnafm_finetune/rnafm_finetune_out/. For another model, change the prefix.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
A table with a header row, tab-separated, or comma-separated if the file name ends in .csv. It needs the columns name and sequence and the label column named by --<prefix>_finetune_label. An empty name, sequence or label stops the run.

name    sequence    te
seq_001 GGGUGCGAU...    1.42
seq_002 AUUCCGAGA...    0.87

Labels are treated as classes if any label is not a number, or if all are whole numbers with at most 10 distinct values; otherwise the task is regression. --<prefix>_finetune_task regression or classification overrides this.

docs.title: Path A: embed and train in one run (default)
docs.text: The workflow embeds the sequence column with the model's own image, then trains the head. It supports the linear and mlp heads.

docs.title: Path B: train on saved embeddings
docs.text:
Give the sequence_embeddings.npy of an earlier run with --<prefix>_finetune_embeddings. The workflow then skips the model and trains the head in the CPU-only rnazoo-finetune-head image. All three heads work, and the sequence column is not needed.

# 1. Embed once; my_seqs.fa holds the table's sequences in the table's order
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --rnafm_input my_seqs.fa --outdir results_emb

# 2. Train heads on the saved embeddings, as often as needed
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --rnafm_finetune_input my_labels.tsv \
  --rnafm_finetune_label te \
  --rnafm_finetune_embeddings results_emb/rnafm/rnafm_out/sequence_embeddings.npy \
  --rnafm_finetune_head_type xgboost

The rows of the .npy must be the table's rows, in the same order. The trainer checks only that the two have the same number of rows.

docs.title: Heads
docs.text:
Set with --<prefix>_finetune_head_type.

Head Architecture Runs in linear (default) One linear layer Path A or B mlp Linear layer to 64 units, ReLU, dropout 0.2, linear output layer Path A or B xgboost XGBoost, up to 200 trees of depth 6 Path B only

The rows are split at random (seed 42) into 80% for training and 20% for validation. The linear and MLP heads train with Adam in batches of 32 and keep the weights with the lowest validation loss, stopping after 5 epochs without improvement. XGBoost stops after 10 rounds without improvement on the validation rows. For the linear and MLP heads, regression labels are standardized on the training rows, and predictions are returned on the original scale.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
In results/<prefix>_finetune/<prefix>_finetune_out/:

  • predictions.tsv: for every row, name, true, predicted and split (train or val); classification adds a prob_<class> column per class.
  • metrics.json: metrics for all rows, the training rows and the validation rows. Regression: MSE, R², Pearson r and Spearman r. Classification: accuracy, macro and weighted F1, AUROC (two classes only), the confusion matrix, and precision, recall and F1 per class.
  • best_head.pt: the linear or MLP head's weights and settings. An XGBoost head is saved as best_head.ubj, with its settings in best_head_config.json.

docs.title: Common parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --<prefix>_finetune_input null Labeled table; setting it starts fine-tuning --<prefix>_finetune_label null Label column (required) --<prefix>_finetune_embeddings null Saved (N, D) embeddings .npy; switches to Path B --<prefix>_finetune_head_type linear linear, mlp or xgboost (Path B only) --<prefix>_finetune_task auto auto, regression or classification --<prefix>_finetune_epochs 20 Maximum epochs for the linear and MLP heads --<prefix>_finetune_lr 1e-3 Learning rate, for Adam or XGBoost --<prefix>_finetune_outdir null Output directory; <outdir>/<prefix>_finetune when unset

docs.title: Test profiles
docs.text:
# Path A, regression; also runs the inference test profile
nextflow run main.nf -profile test_finetune,docker,cpu

# Path B, regression
nextflow run main.nf -profile test_finetune_from_emb,docker,cpu

# Path B, classification of two classes
nextflow run main.nf -profile test_finetune_classify,docker,cpu

Each covers eight of the nine models (all but HydraRNA) on 30 sequences whose labels follow GC content; under cpu, test_finetune skips Orthrus. Path B uses a random embedding file, so the tests check that every step runs and the metrics are finite, not how well the heads learn.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only the head trains; the foundation models cannot be fine-tuned themselves.
  • XGBoost needs saved embeddings; without them the workflow stops with an error.
  • One label per row; multi-label classification is not supported.
  • Classes are not reweighted, so a rare class weighs only as much as its rows.
  • There is no hyperparameter search, and the validation fraction, patience and batch size are fixed.
  • The validation rows also choose when training stops, so they are not an independent test. For a held-out test set, run finetune_head.py --split-file (one train or test per row) in the rnazoo-finetune-head image; the workflow does not pass a split file.
  • The head accepts any (N, D) array and does not check which model made it.

docs.title: Other fine-tuning
docs.text:
• RiboTIE: every run fine-tunes the pretrained models on the sample's reads before it calls ORFs. --ribotie_max_epochs and --ribotie_patience control the training.
  • RiboNN: transfer learning from the pretrained human model to a new TE column, with cross-validation.
  • UTR-LM: trains the model and its head on 5' UTRs with a numeric label.

RiboNN and UTR-LM fine-tuning currently fail, and neither is in a test profile: conf/test.config records a shape mismatch in upstream RiboNN's validation step and a batch-format error in the UTR-LM script. A fix is planned for a later release.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Nextflow 23.04.0 or later, which needs Java.
  • Docker, or Singularity or Apptainer, to run the model images.
  • For GPU runs, an NVIDIA GPU, and for Docker also the NVIDIA Container Toolkit: the gpu profile starts containers with --runtime=nvidia, which the toolkit provides. With Singularity, the gpu profile passes --nv instead.

Orthrus, HydraRNA and DRfold2 run only on a GPU. The other 20 models also run on the CPU.

docs.title: Install Nextflow
docs.text:
curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash
sudo mv nextflow /usr/local/bin/

Or with conda:

conda install -c bioconda nextflow

docs.title: Get the pipeline
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ericmalekos/RNA-Zoo.git
cd RNA-Zoo

docs.title: Container images
docs.text:
The images are on GitHub Container Registry as ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-<name>. Nextflow pulls the images of the models you run when it first needs them, so pulling ahead is optional. With Singularity, Nextflow converts each image on first use; set NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR to a directory with space to keep the converted images for later runs.

The gpu profile uses the CUDA images, rnazoo-<name>; the cpu profile uses the smaller rnazoo-<name>-cpu. The exceptions:

  • ERNIE-RNA has one image, rnazoo-ernierna, for both profiles.
  • Orthrus, HydraRNA and DRfold2 have only a GPU image and are skipped under cpu.
  • TranslationAI runs rnazoo-translationai-cpu under both profiles, because its command-line tool hides the GPU.
  • Fine-tuning on saved embeddings runs in the CPU-only rnazoo-finetune-head.

The 23 images of the gpu profile add up to about 98 GB compressed, the 20 of the cpu profile to about 32 GB; layers that images share are downloaded once. To pull a whole set ahead of time:

# Images of the gpu profile
for img in ribonn riboformer tristan translationai-cpu saluki codontransformer \
           rnafm rinalmo ernierna orthrus hydrarna rnaernie plantrnafm calm mrnabert \
           rhofold spotrna drfold2 multirm pangolin spliceai splicebert utrlm; do
  docker pull ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-${img}:latest
done

# Images of the cpu profile
for img in ribonn-cpu riboformer-cpu tristan-cpu translationai-cpu saluki-cpu \
           codontransformer-cpu rnafm-cpu rinalmo-cpu ernierna rnaernie-cpu plantrnafm-cpu \
           calm-cpu mrnabert-cpu rhofold-cpu spotrna-cpu multirm-cpu pangolin-cpu \
           spliceai-cpu splicebert-cpu utrlm-cpu; do
  docker pull ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-${img}:latest
done

The :latest tags move with every change. To run the exact images of a release, add its digest-pinned config, which works with either profile:

nextflow -c conf/containers_v1.0.1.config run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --rnafm_input input.fa

To run the images without Nextflow, see Direct Docker usage.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Combine a container engine, a device and, optionally, a test profile, for example -profile test,docker,cpu.

Profile Effect docker Run the images with Docker singularity Run the images with Singularity or Apptainer gpu GPU images, with the GPU passed to the containers cpu CPU images; GPU-only models are skipped with a warning test Test inputs from tests/data/ for 19 models: all but Orthrus, HydraRNA, RhoFold and DRfold2 test_gpu test plus RhoFold and Orthrus test_singularity Test inputs for five models (RiboNN, RNA-FM, SpliceBERT, MultiRM, UTR-LM) test_finetune, test_finetune_from_emb, test_finetune_classify Fine-tuning tests; see Fine Tuning

Always give gpu or cpu. With neither, the pipeline uses the GPU images but passes no GPU to them.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
# With an NVIDIA GPU: 21 models
nextflow run main.nf -profile test_gpu,docker,gpu

# Without one: 19 models on the CPU images
nextflow run main.nf -profile test,docker,cpu

# With Singularity or Apptainer: five models
nextflow run main.nf -profile test_singularity,singularity,cpu

Every process should finish with a check mark, and the outputs land in results_test/. RhoFold is left out of test because it is slow on the CPU. HydraRNA and DRfold2 are in no test profile.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Run these commands in the cloned repository (Installation). They use the CPU images; with an NVIDIA GPU, write gpu instead of cpu in the profile. Orthrus, HydraRNA and DRfold2 need a GPU and are skipped under cpu.

docs.title: Run one model
docs.text:
A model runs only when its input is set, so there is nothing to switch off.

# RNA embeddings (RNA-FM)
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --rnafm_input my_rna.fa

# Translation efficiency (RiboNN): a TSV of 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR sequences
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --ribonn_input my_transcripts.tsv

# RNA 3D structure (RhoFold)
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --rhofold_input my_rna.fa

# RNA modifications (MultiRM)
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --multirm_input my_rna.fa

Each model's page gives its input format and parameters.

docs.title: Run several models
docs.text:
Set several inputs and the models run in parallel:

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --rnafm_input sequences.fa \
  --spotrna_input sequences.fa \
  --multirm_input sequences.fa

docs.title: Output directory and CPUs
docs.text:
Each model writes to <outdir>/<model>/, with results/ as the default --outdir; --<model>_outdir moves one model's results. Each task gets --task_cpus CPUs (default 4), and the thread limits inside the containers follow it.

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --rnafm_input sequences.fa \
  --outdir my_project/results \
  --task_cpus 8

The results are laid out by model:

results/
  ribonn/
    ribonn_out/
      prediction_output.txt
  rnafm/
    rnafm_out/
      sequence_embeddings.npy
      labels.txt
  spotrna/
    spotrna_out/
      structures.txt
  ...

docs.title: Parameters file
docs.text:
For many parameters, write them to a YAML file and pass it with -params-file. nextflow.config lists every parameter with its default.

outdir: my_results
rnafm_input: data/rna_sequences.fa
rnafm_per_token: true
multirm_input: data/rna_sequences.fa
multirm_alpha: 0.01

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu -params-file my_params.yml

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text:
The nine foundation models can train a prediction head on your labeled sequences:

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --rnafm_finetune_input my_labels.tsv \
  --rnafm_finetune_label te

See Fine Tuning. The fine-tuning modules of RiboNN and UTR-LM currently fail.

docs.title: Without Nextflow
docs.text: Each image also runs with a plain docker run; see Direct Docker usage.

docs.title: CaLM
docs.text:
Extract codon-level embeddings of protein-coding sequences.

  • Paper: Nature Machine Intelligence 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/oxpig/CaLM
  • License: BSD-3-Clause (code). The weights, downloaded from opig.stats.ox.ac.uk, carry no license statement in the repository or the paper, so their commercial use and redistribution are unclear.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-calm-cpu and rnazoo-calm).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: CaLM is a 12-layer transformer encoder (width 768, rotary positions, 85.7 million parameters) that reads a coding sequence one codon per token. It was pretrained by masked language modeling on 9 million non-redundant coding sequences from the European Nucleotide Archive, cropped to 1,024 codons. The wrapper returns one 768-d embedding per sequence (the mean over codons) and optionally one per codon.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA of coding sequences. The wrapper reads each sequence as codons from its first base, so give the CDS alone, in frame: UTRs would be read as codons too. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U. A length that is not a multiple of 3 is trimmed to the last full codon, and sequences over 1,024 codons (3,072 nt) are truncated, both with a warning. Empty sequences are skipped.

Example (tests/data/rnafm_test.fa, a smoke input rather than real CDSs; the first sequence is trimmed from 103 to 102 nt):

>test_rna_1
GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGG...
>test_rna_2
AUUCCGAGAGCUAACGGAGAACUCUGUUCGAUUU...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In calm_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, 768), one row per sequence (<cls> and <eos> excluded from the mean)
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (C + 2, 768) for C codons; unlike the mean, it keeps <cls> (first row) and <eos> (last row). Spaces and / in the header become _.

Example, for the input above:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("calm_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (2, 768)
names = open("calm_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # ['test_rna_1', 'test_rna_2']

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-calm-cpu:latest \
  calm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-calm:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Add --per-token for per-codon embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --calm_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/calm/calm_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --calm_input null FASTA file of coding sequences --calm_per_token false Also write per-codon embeddings --calm_max_codons 1024 Truncate longer sequences to this many codons

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: Train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on frozen CaLM embeddings, as the Fine Tuning guide describes. Its common parameters take the prefix calm: --calm_finetune_input and --calm_finetune_label are required, and --calm_finetune_embeddings reuses saved embeddings. Put in-frame coding sequences in the sequence column.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • The wrapper does not locate the CDS; give in-frame coding sequences.

docs.title: CodonTransformer
docs.text:
Optimize codon usage for protein sequences across 164 organisms.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/Adibvafa/CodonTransformer
  • License: Apache 2.0
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-codontransformer-cpu and rnazoo-codontransformer).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A BigBird transformer writes a DNA coding sequence for each protein, with codons chosen for the target organism. The base model was trained on about 1 million genes from 164 organisms; the image holds the fine-tuned model (highly expressed genes of 13 organisms and two chloroplast genomes).

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA of protein sequences; proteins over 2,046 amino acids are truncated without a warning. The organism must be spelled as one of the 164 entries of ORGANISM2ID in upstream's CodonUtils.py, for example Homo sapiens, Mus musculus or Escherichia coli general; other names stop the run.

>test_protein_1
MALWMRLLPLLALLALWGPDPAAAFVN

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
optimized_codons.fa: one DNA coding sequence per protein, under the same header, ending in a stop codon. Example (tests/data/codontransformer_test.fa, Homo sapiens, test profile):

>test_protein_1
ATGGCCCTGTGGATGAGGCTGCTGCCCCTGCTGGCCCTGCTGGCCCTGTGGGGCCCTGACCCTGCTGCCGCCTTTGTGAACTGA

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-codontransformer-cpu:latest \
  codon_transformer_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out/optimized_codons.fa --organism "Homo sapiens"

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-codontransformer:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Add --no-deterministic to sample codons.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --codontransformer_input /path/to/input.fa \
  --codontransformer_organism "Homo sapiens"

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/codontransformer/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --codontransformer_input null Protein FASTA --codontransformer_organism Homo sapiens Target organism, spelled as in upstream's list --codontransformer_deterministic true true takes the most likely codons; false samples

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • A command-line --codontransformer_deterministic false can reach the module as the string false, which it treats as true. To sample, set codontransformer_deterministic: false in a -params-file.

docs.title: DRfold2
docs.text:
Predict RNA 3D structure from a single sequence, without alignments or templates.

  • Paper: PLOS Biology 2026
  • Upstream: https://github.com/leeyang/DRfold2
  • License: MIT, as stated in the upstream README (the repository has no LICENSE file). The model weights carry no license statement, and the bundled Arena refinement tool declares no license. The RNA-Zoo image is redistributed with the permission of the model's authors.
  • Device: GPU only (image rnazoo-drfold2); skipped with a warning under -profile cpu.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: DRfold2 combines a pretrained RNA composite language model (RCLM) with a denoising structure module. Four configurations of 20 checkpoints each predict end-to-end models and geometry restraints (334.9 million parameters with the RCLM). A post-processing step selects the best model and optimizes it with those potentials, and Arena rebuilds the full-atom model. RNA-Zoo runs each FASTA record as a separate DRfold2 job.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U; empty sequences are skipped. There is no length cap; time and memory grow with length.

Example (tests/data/drfold2_test.fa, a 24-nt UUCG hairpin):

>uucg_hairpin
GAGCGGCAUCUUCGGAUGCCGCUC

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In drfold2_out/, one PDB per sequence, named after its header (/, spaces and : become _): <name>.pdb is the top model (upstream's relax/model_1.pdb). With clustering on, the alternative models follow as <name>_alt2.pdb, <name>_alt3.pdb and so on; upstream makes up to five models in all.

Example, for the input above: drfold2_out/uucg_hairpin.pdb, which opens in PyMOL, ChimeraX or Biopython.

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \
  -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-drfold2:latest \
  drfold2_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

Add --cluster for the alternative models, and --keep-intermediate to keep each sequence's working directory (_drfold2_work_<name>/ in the output directory).

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,gpu --drfold2_input /path/to/input.fa

Results go to results/drfold2/drfold2_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --drfold2_input null FASTA file --drfold2_cluster false Also write alternative models from a clustering pass --drfold2_keep_intermediate false Keep each sequence's working directory; it stays in the Nextflow task directory and is not published

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• An error on any sequence stops the run.
  • Upstream's optional OpenMM refinement (script/refine.py) is not available: the image has no OpenMM.

docs.title: ERNIE-RNA
docs.text:
Extract structure-aware RNA embeddings from a language model with a base-pairing attention bias.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/Bruce-ywj/ERNIE-RNA
  • License: MIT (code). The pretrained weights carry no license statement (the README's license sentence names the source code only), so their commercial use and redistribution are unclear.
  • Device: CPU or GPU; one image, rnazoo-ernierna, serves both profiles.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: ERNIE-RNA is a 12-layer BERT-style encoder (width 768, 86 million parameters) whose attention carries a base-pairing bias. It was pretrained by masked language modeling on 20.4 million non-coding RNAs from RNAcentral. The wrapper returns the last layer's CLS token as a 768-d sequence embedding, and optionally one embedding per nucleotide.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U. Sequences over 1,022 nt, the upstream maximum, are truncated with a warning; empty sequences are skipped.

Example (tests/data/rnafm_test.fa, sequences shortened):

>test_rna_1
GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGG...
>test_rna_2
AUUCCGAGAGCUAACGGAGAACUCUGUUCGAUUU...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In ernierna_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, 768), one row per sequence
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (L, 768), for each sequence (spaces and / in the header become _)

Example, for the input above:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("ernierna_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (2, 768)
names = open("ernierna_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # ['test_rna_1', 'test_rna_2']

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-ernierna:latest \
  ernierna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For a GPU, add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all (same image). Add --per-token for per-nucleotide embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --ernierna_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for a GPU. Results go to results/ernierna/ernierna_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --ernierna_input null FASTA file --ernierna_per_token false Also write per-nucleotide embeddings --ernierna_max_len 1022 Truncate longer sequences to this many nt

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: Train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on frozen ERNIE-RNA embeddings, as the Fine Tuning guide describes. Its common parameters take the prefix ernierna: --ernierna_finetune_input and --ernierna_finetune_label are required, and --ernierna_finetune_embeddings reuses saved embeddings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The sequence embedding is the CLS token; the other RNA-Zoo embedding models average over positions.
  • Upstream's secondary structure, 3D closeness and mean ribosome load models are not included.

docs.title: HydraRNA
docs.text:
Extract embeddings of full-length RNAs from a hybrid state-space and attention language model.

  • Paper: Genome Biology 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/GuipengLi/HydraRNA
  • License: MIT (code and weights)
  • Device: GPU only (image rnazoo-hydrarna); skipped with a warning under -profile cpu.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: HydraRNA has 12 layers of width 1,024 (84 million parameters): bidirectional Hydra state-space layers, with attention in the 6th and 12th. It was pretrained by masked language modeling on 28 million non-coding RNAs and mRNAs, with sequences over 4,096 nt split into segments. The image holds the base model from the authors' Zenodo record 20481998. The wrapper runs it in float16 and returns one 1024-d embedding per sequence, the mean over its nucleotide positions, and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA; T becomes U. The model reads at most 10,240 nt per pass, so longer sequences are split into 10,240 nt chunks and their embeddings averaged. Nothing is truncated.

Example (tests/data/rnafm_test.fa, sequences shortened):

>test_rna_1
GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGG...
>test_rna_2
AUUCCGAGAGCUAACGGAGAACUCUGUUCGAUUU...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In hydrarna_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, 1024), one row per sequence
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (L, 1024), covering at most the first 10,240 nt (spaces and / in the header become _)

Example, for the input above:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("hydrarna_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (2, 1024)
names = open("hydrarna_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # ['test_rna_1', 'test_rna_2']

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \
  -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-hydrarna:latest \
  hydrarna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

Add --per-token for per-nucleotide embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,gpu --hydrarna_input /path/to/input.fa

Results go to results/hydrarna/hydrarna_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --hydrarna_input null FASTA file --hydrarna_per_token false Also write per-nucleotide embeddings --hydrarna_max_len 10000 Print a note for sequences longer than this (no truncation)

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: Train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on frozen HydraRNA embeddings, as the Fine Tuning guide describes. Its common parameters take the prefix hydrarna: --hydrarna_finetune_input and --hydrarna_finetune_label are required, and --hydrarna_finetune_embeddings reuses saved embeddings. The full chain needs a GPU (skipped under -profile cpu); with --hydrarna_finetune_embeddings, the head trains on CPU in the rnazoo-finetune-head image.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Needs a CUDA GPU; there is no CPU image.
  • Chunks are averaged with equal weight, so a short last chunk counts as much as a full one.
  • Upstream's HydraRNA_model_V2.pt and secondary structure model are not included.

docs.title: MultiRM
docs.text:
Predict sites of 12 RNA modification types from sequence.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2021
  • Upstream: https://github.com/Tsedao/MultiRM
  • License: MIT
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-multirm-cpu and rnazoo-multirm).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: MultiRM scores each position of an RNA for 12 modifications: Am, Cm, Gm and Um (2'-O-methylation), m1A, m5C, m5U, m6A, m6Am, m7G, Psi (pseudouridine) and AtoI (A-to-I editing). The 51-nt window around the position is read as 49 overlapping 3-mers (word2vec embeddings) by a bidirectional LSTM with attention and 12 task heads (2.1 million parameters), trained on 20 base-resolution epitranscriptome profiles from 15 technologies.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Sequences shorter than 51 nt are skipped with a warning; U becomes T. The first and last 25 nt of each sequence are not scored.

Example (tests/data/multirm_test.fa):

>test_rna_modification
GGGGCCGTGGATACCTGCCTTTTAATTCTTTTTTATTCGCCCATCGGGGCCGCGGATACCTGCTTTTTATTTTTTTTTCCTTAGCCCATCGGGG

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In multirm_out/:

  • modification_scores.tsv: one row per scored position (1-based), with its base and the 12 probabilities
  • predicted_sites.tsv: each position and modification with a p-value below the cutoff; the p-value is the fraction of upstream's stored null scores (neg_prob.csv) above the score
  • with plotting on: a heatmap per sequence, <header>_modifications.png (/ and spaces become _)

Example rows, from a run on ATF4 (ENST00000674920.3):

header  position    base    Am  Cm  Gm  ... m7G Psi AtoI
ATF4|ENST00000674920.3  27  G   0.000019    0.000000    0.434129    ... 0.373000    0.000266    0.000000

header  modification    position    base    probability p_value
ATF4|ENST00000674920.3  m6A 601 A   0.693416    0.040000

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-multirm-cpu:latest \
  multirm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-multirm:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. The wrapper takes --alpha (default 0.05) and --plot.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --multirm_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/multirm/multirm_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --multirm_input null FASTA file --multirm_alpha 0.05 p-value cutoff for predicted_sites.tsv --multirm_plot false Also write per-sequence heatmaps

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • Scores differ from those of upstream's Scripts/main.py, which transposes the 3-mer input so that each score depends only on the window's first 3-mer. The RNA-Zoo wrapper passes the whole window.

docs.title: Orthrus
docs.text:
Embed mature mRNAs with a Mamba-based foundation model.

  • Paper: Nature Methods 2026
  • Upstream: https://github.com/bowang-lab/Orthrus
  • License: MIT (code and weights)
  • Device: GPU only (image rnazoo-orthrus, with all seven checkpoints); skipped with a warning under -profile cpu.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Orthrus is a Mamba state-space encoder of mature mRNA, pretrained by contrastive learning on splice isoforms from ten metazoans and orthologous transcripts from over 400 mammals. The default checkpoint, large-4track, has 6 layers of width 512 (10.2 million parameters). The wrapper returns one embedding per sequence, the mean over its positions, and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
Choose a checkpoint with --orthrus_variant.

Variant Hugging Face repo Width Notes large-4track (default) quietflamingo/orthrus-large-4-track 512 4track antichronology/orthrus-4-track 512 Fails at ortholog retrieval and at coding versus noncoding classification base-4track quietflamingo/orthrus-base-4-track 256 6track antichronology/orthrus-6-track 512 small-6track antichronology/orthrus-small-6-track 256 mlm-6track antichronology/orthrus-mlm-6-track 512 Contrastive plus masked language modeling large-6track quietflamingo/orthrus-large-6-track 512

4-track variants read A, C, G and T as one-hot tracks and need only the FASTA. 6-track variants also need annotation for two more tracks: a 1 at the first nucleotide of each CDS codon, and a 1 at the last nucleotide of every exon but the last.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA (plain or .gz) of complete mature mRNAs (5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR); T or U both work. There is no length cap and no truncation. The wrapper warns, without refusing, about sequences shorter than --orthrus_min_len.

Example: tests/data/orthrus_test.fa, two synthetic mRNAs of 457 and 439 nt.

docs.title: Annotation input for 6-track variants
docs.text:
Give one of:

  • --orthrus_annotation: a TSV (or CSV) with a header row and the columns name, cds_start and cds_end (0-based transcript coordinates, end exclusive), plus optional exon_lengths (comma-separated, in transcript order; without it the splice track is all zeros). name is the FASTA ID (the header's first word, before any |) without a version suffix.
  • --orthrus_gtf: a GENCODE or Ensembl GTF (plain or .gz), from which the wrapper derives each transcript's CDS and exon lengths, matching IDs without version suffixes.

If both are given, the TSV is used. Sequences without annotation are skipped with a warning, so the output can have fewer rows than the FASTA.

name    cds_start   cds_end exon_lengths
tx1 78  1578    78,450,123,50,899

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In orthrus_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, D), with D the variant's width (512 or 256)
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (L, D), for each sequence (spaces and / in the header become _)

Example, for tests/data/orthrus_test.fa with the default variant:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("orthrus_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (2, 512)
names = open("orthrus_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # full headers: 'test_mrna_1 synthetic ...'

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \
  -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-orthrus:latest \
  orthrus_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For a 6-track variant, mount the annotation and add, for example, --variant 6track --annotation /data/annotation.tsv (or --gtf /data/annotation.gtf.gz). Add --per-token for per-nucleotide embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,gpu --orthrus_input /path/to/input.fa

# 6-track variant, annotation derived from a GTF
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,gpu \
  --orthrus_input /path/to/input.fa \
  --orthrus_variant 6track \
  --orthrus_gtf /path/to/gencode.gtf.gz

Results go to results/orthrus/orthrus_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --orthrus_input null FASTA file --orthrus_variant large-4track Checkpoint (see Variants) --orthrus_annotation null Annotation TSV for 6-track variants --orthrus_gtf null GTF for 6-track variants --orthrus_per_token false Also write per-nucleotide embeddings --orthrus_min_len 200 Warn about sequences shorter than this many nt

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: Train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on frozen Orthrus embeddings, as the Fine Tuning guide describes. Its common parameters take the prefix orthrus: --orthrus_finetune_input and --orthrus_finetune_label are required, and --orthrus_finetune_embeddings reuses saved embeddings. The full chain needs a GPU (skipped under -profile cpu) and always embeds with large-4track, whatever --orthrus_variant says. With --orthrus_finetune_embeddings, the head trains on CPU in the rnazoo-finetune-head image, so embeddings from any variant work.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Needs a CUDA GPU; there is no CPU image.
  • Orthrus was trained on full mature transcripts; fragments such as CDS-only sequences or single exons are out of distribution.
  • With --orthrus_gtf, a transcript without CDS records gets a CDS track along its whole length.

docs.title: Pangolin
docs.text:
Predict how genetic variants change splice-site strength, with models trained on four tissues.

  • Paper: Genome Biology 2022
  • Upstream: https://github.com/tkzeng/Pangolin
  • License: GPL-3.0, a copyleft license, for the code and the models it ships. Public Docker distribution is permitted (the Dockerfile is in this repository, and rebuilders are bound by the same license); commercial users should review the GPL-3.0 redistribution clauses for their use.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-pangolin-cpu and rnazoo-pangolin).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Pangolin is a dilated residual convolutional network trained on splice-site usage from RNA-seq of heart, liver, brain and testis in human, rhesus macaque, mouse and rat. Twelve models (three per tissue) read 5,000 nt on each side of a variant and score each position within --pangolin_distance of it; each position keeps its largest change across tissues.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
1. Variants: a VCF, or a CSV with a header row and the columns CHROM,POS,REF,ALT (other names via --pangolin_column_ids). The file name must end in .vcf or .csv; compressed files are not read.
  2. A reference FASTA, plain or gzipped. Pangolin reads it with pyfastx, which builds its own index.
  3. A gffutils annotation database, built once from a GTF with upstream's create_db.py, which the image includes:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/gtf_dir:/work \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-pangolin-cpu:latest \
  python /opt/conda/envs/pangolin/bin/create_db.py /work/gencode.v38.annotation.gtf.gz
# writes /work/gencode.v38.annotation.db

By default create_db.py keeps only transcripts tagged Ensembl_canonical (--filter None keeps all). The upstream README links prebuilt GENCODE release 38 databases for GRCh38 and GRCh37.

Example VCF (upstream examples/brca.vcf, GRCh37):

##fileformat=VCFv4.2
#CHROM  POS ID  REF ALT QUAL    FILTER  INFO
chr17   41276135    .   T   G   .   .   .

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
pangolin_out/<input name>.pangolin.vcf (or .csv): the input, with a Pangolin INFO field (VCF) or column (CSV) holding one entry per overlapping gene, gene_id|pos:largest_increase|pos:largest_decrease|Warnings:. Positions are relative to the variant. With --pangolin_score_cutoff, every position whose change reaches the cutoff is listed instead of the largest two.

Example (a ZEB2 variant from a GRCh38 CSV run with --pangolin_distance 500; scores are rounded to two decimals but can print with extra digits):

CHROM,POS,REF,ALT,Pangolin
chr2,144401198,C,T,ENSG00000169554.24|-12:0.5299999713897705|1:-0.8600000143051147|Warnings:

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/inputs:/work \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-pangolin-cpu:latest \
  pangolin_predict.py -i /work/variants.vcf -r /work/genome.fa \
    -a /work/annotation.db -o /work/variants.pangolin

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-pangolin:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Pangolin adds .vcf or .csv to the output prefix.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --pangolin_variants /path/to/variants.vcf \
  --pangolin_reference_fasta /path/to/genome.fa \
  --pangolin_annotation_db /path/to/annotation.db

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/pangolin/pangolin_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --pangolin_variants null VCF or CSV of variants --pangolin_reference_fasta null Reference FASTA; required --pangolin_annotation_db null gffutils database; required --pangolin_distance 50 Positions scored on each side of the variant --pangolin_mask 'True' True sets gains at annotated sites and losses at unannotated sites to 0 --pangolin_score_cutoff null List every position with an absolute change at or above this value --pangolin_column_ids null CSV only: chromosome, position, REF and ALT column names (CHROM,POS,REF,ALT when unset)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only substitutions and simple indels (REF or ALT a single base) are scored, and in a VCF only the first ALT allele of each record.
  • Variants get no scores when they lie outside annotated genes, within 5,000 nt of a chromosome end, are deletions longer than twice --pangolin_distance, or do not match the reference.
  • Scores are not reported per tissue.

docs.title: PlantRNA-FM
docs.text:
Extract RNA embeddings from a language model pretrained on plant transcriptomes.

  • Paper: Nature Machine Intelligence 2024
  • Upstream: Hugging Face yangheng/PlantRNA-FM
  • License: MIT (weights, per the Hugging Face model card); the image holds no PlantRNA-FM code.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-plantrnafm-cpu and rnazoo-plantrnafm).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: PlantRNA-FM is a 12-layer ESM-style transformer encoder (width 480, rotary positions, 33.8 million parameters). It was pretrained on protein-coding transcripts of 1,124 plant species (the 1KP dataset, about 25 million sequences) by masked nucleotide modeling plus prediction of secondary structure and of UTR and CDS regions. The wrapper returns one 480-d embedding per sequence (the mean over nucleotides) and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U. Sequences over 1,024 nt are truncated with a warning (1,026 tokens with the start and end tokens, the maximum the paper set for fine-tuning); empty sequences are skipped.

Example (tests/data/rnafm_test.fa, used by the test profile; sequences shortened):

>test_rna_1
GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGG...
>test_rna_2

docs.title: RNAErnie
docs.text:
Extract RNA embeddings from RNAErnie, an RNA language model built on the ERNIE framework.

  • Paper: Nature Machine Intelligence 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/CatIIIIIIII/RNAErnie; weights: Hugging Face LLM-EDA/RNAErnie
  • License: MIT for the original PaddlePaddle code, which the image does not include; Apache-2.0 for the LLM-EDA/RNAErnie weights that it loads.

The wrapper returns one 768-d embedding per sequence (the mean over nucleotides) and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: RhoFold+
docs.text:
Predict RNA 3D structure from a single sequence.

  • Paper: Nature Methods 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/ml4bio/RhoFold
  • License: Apache 2.0
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-rhofold-cpu and rnazoo-rhofold).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RhoFold+ predicts a full-atom 3D structure with a transformer and an invariant point attention structure module, fed by a built-in RNA-FM language model, over 10 recycling passes (126.9 million parameters). RNA-Zoo runs the single-sequence mode: no MSA is built or read.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U. Each sequence must be at most 1,022 nt, the limit of the built-in RNA-FM; the wrapper does not truncate.

Example (tests/data/rhofold_test.fa):

>tRNA_fragment
GCGGAUUUAGCUCAGUUGGGAGAGCGCCAGACUGAAGAUCUGGAGGUCCUGUGUUCGAUCCACAGAAUUCGCACCA

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
One directory per sequence, named after the first word of its header (/ and : become _):

  • unrelaxed_model.pdb: the 3D model, with pLDDT × 100 in the B-factor column
  • ss.ct: the secondary structure (pairs with probability above 0.5)
  • results.npz: distograms (dist_n, dist_p, dist_c), the base-pair probability map (ss_prob_map) and per-residue pLDDT from 0 to 1 (plddt)
  • log.txt: the run log

Example, for the input above:

import numpy as np
plddt = np.load("rhofold_out/tRNA_fragment/results.npz")["plddt"][0]  # one value per residue

docs.text: Parameter Default Description --rhofold_input null FASTA file --rhofold_relax_steps 0 Amber relaxation steps; leave at 0 (see Limitations)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No Amber relaxation: the images lack OpenMM, so --rhofold_relax_steps above 0 makes each sequence fail after its unrelaxed outputs are written.
  • The PDB B-factors are shifted by one residue (upstream writes each pLDDT on the next residue, the last on the first); read per-residue pLDDT from results.npz.
  • A failed sequence, for example one over 1,022 nt, gets a warning; the others still run.

docs.title: RiNALMo
docs.text:
Extract RNA embeddings from a 650M-parameter RNA language model.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/lbcb-sci/RiNALMo
  • License: Apache-2.0 (code), CC BY 4.0 (weights)
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-rinalmo-cpu and rnazoo-rinalmo).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RiNALMo is a 33-layer transformer encoder (width 1,280, 650 million parameters, rotary position embeddings) pretrained by masked language modeling on 36 million non-coding RNA sequences from RNAcentral and other databases. The image runs the giga model, built from upstream's non_flash branch, which needs no FlashAttention. The wrapper returns one 1280-d embedding per sequence, the mean over its nucleotide positions, and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: RiboNN
docs.text:
Predict translation efficiency (TE) from mRNA sequence for 78 human cell types and tissues.

  • Paper: Nature Biotechnology 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/Sanofi-Public/RiboNN
  • License: Sanofi academic, non-commercial license for the code (LICENSE) and the weights (MODEL WEIGHTS LICENSE). The grant covers use, copying, modification and merging for academic or non-profit, non-commercial purposes only. The RNA-Zoo image is redistributed with the permission of the model's authors; anyone using it is bound by these terms.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-ribonn-cpu and rnazoo-ribonn).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RiboNN is a convolutional network trained on TE from 1,076 human and 835 mouse ribosome profiling samples with matched RNA-seq. From an mRNA's 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR it predicts TE in all 78 human cell types at once (68 with the mouse model). A human prediction averages 50 models.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
Tab-separated, with a header row and the columns tx_id, utr5_sequence, cds_sequence (start through stop codon) and utr3_sequence. Each CDS must be a multiple of 3 nt and end in a stop codon, or the run fails. Transcripts over 12,288 nt, or with a 5' UTR over 1,381 nt or a CDS plus 3' UTR over 11,937 nt, are dropped from the output.

Example (tests/data/ribonn_prediction_input.txt, sequences shortened):

tx_id   utr5_sequence   cds_sequence    utr3_sequence
ENST00000215375.7   AGACGTCCCTGCGCGTCG...   ATGCTGCCCGCCGCGCTG...   GCGGTGCGTACCCGGTGT...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
ribonn_out/prediction_output.txt, tab-separated: the input columns, one predicted_TE_<cell type> column per cell type, and mean_predicted_TE (the mean over cell types). Values are on the paper's TE scale, a log-ratio residual, not log2 TE.

Example (sequence columns omitted):

tx_id   predicted_TE_HEK293 predicted_TE_HeLa   ... mean_predicted_TE
ENST00000215375.7   1.0705105   1.0321615   ... 1.0564895

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.tsv:/data/input.tsv \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-ribonn-cpu:latest \
  bash -c "cd /app && python3 /opt/bin/ribonn_predict.py -i /data/input.tsv -o /out --species human"

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-ribonn:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. For a fine-tuned checkpoint, mount it and add --checkpoint <file> --target <column>.

docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --ribonn_input /path/to/input.tsv

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/ribonn/ribonn_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --ribonn_input null Input table --ribonn_species human human or mouse models; ignored with --ribonn_checkpoint --ribonn_checkpoint null Absolute path to a fine-tuned .ckpt, used instead of the pretrained models --ribonn_finetune_target null With --ribonn_checkpoint: the column the checkpoint was trained on; names the output column

docs.title: Fine-tuning on your own data
docs.text:
Transfer learning from the pretrained human model to one new TE column, such as a new cell type. The input is the prediction table plus a numeric target column; rows without a value are dropped.

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --ribonn_finetune_input my_training_data.tsv \
  --ribonn_finetune_target TE_MyCondition
Parameter Default Description --ribonn_finetune_input null Training table --ribonn_finetune_target null (required) Column with the TE values --ribonn_finetune_phase1_epochs 50 Phase 1: new head on frozen convolution layers --ribonn_finetune_phase2_epochs 150 Phase 2: all layers, learning rate cut tenfold to 1e-5 --ribonn_finetune_patience 50 Phase 2 early stopping on validation R² --ribonn_finetune_folds 5 Cross-validation folds

Outputs in results/ribonn_finetune/ribonn_finetune_out/:

  • predictions.tsv: tx_id, fold and predicted_<target>, each transcript predicted while held out
  • fold<k>/: the checkpoint with the best validation R² in fold k

To predict with one of these checkpoints, run the prediction with --ribonn_checkpoint (an absolute path, since the module runs from /app) and --ribonn_finetune_target. The output then holds tx_id and predicted_<target> only.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Fine-tuning starts from the human model only.
  • Fine-tuning is not in the test profile: conf/test.config records that it failed on tests/data/ribonn_finetune.tsv in upstream RiboNN's validation_step.

docs.title: RiboTIE (TRISTAN)
docs.text:
Detect translated ORFs from ribosome profiling reads with a transformer model.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/TRISTAN-ORF/TRISTAN (v1.1.1)
  • License: MIT (code and weights)
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-tristan-cpu and rnazoo-tristan).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: RiboTIE scores every transcript position as a translation start from the ribosome profiling reads, with a Performer transformer. Two human models, pretrained on eight datasets and split by chromosome into complementary folds, are fine-tuned on each sample before predicting and listing the called ORFs.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
A directory with the genome FASTA, a GTF and, per sample, a BAM or SAM of reads mapped to the transcriptome; plus a YAML config. The module copies the directory to data/, so config paths start with data/, and sets h5_path and out_prefix itself. Transcripts over 30,000 nt are skipped.

Example (tests/data/ribotie_config.yml, shortened):

gtf_path : data/GRCh38v110_snippet.gtf
fa_path  : data/GRCh38v110_snippet.fa
h5_path  : ribotie_out/dbs/ribotie.h5
out_prefix : ribotie_out/out/ribotie
ribo_paths :
  SRR000001 : data/SRR000001.bam
  SRR000002 : data/SRR000002.bam

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In results/ribotie/ribotie_out/out/, per sample: ribotie_<sample>.csv and .gtf with the called ORFs (.novel.* for novel ORFs, .redundant.* before upstream's CDS variant filter), .npy with raw scores for every position, and the fine-tuned models (_f0.rt.ckpt, _f1.rt.ckpt, _params.rt.yml). ribotie_out/dbs/ribotie.h5 holds the parsed inputs.

Example (ribotie_SRR000001.csv from the test profile, first columns):

ribotie_score,ribotie_rank,seqname,ORF_id,ORF_len,transcript_id,transcript_len,start_codon,stop_codon,strand,ORF_type,...
0.6596,1,1,ENST00000673477_121,1944,ENST00000673477,4098,ATG,TAG,+,annotated CDS,...

docs.text:
From a directory holding config.yml and the inputs in data/:

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v "$PWD":/work -w /work \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-tristan-cpu:latest \
  bash -c "mkdir -p ribotie_out/dbs ribotie_out/out && ribotie config.yml --accelerator cpu --overwrite_data"

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-tristan:latest, add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and pass --accelerator gpu.

docs.text:
