  --ribotie_input /path/to/data \
  --ribotie_config /path/to/config.yml

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/ribotie/ribotie_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --ribotie_input null Directory with the FASTA, GTF and read files --ribotie_config null YAML config (required with --ribotie_input) --ribotie_max_epochs null Maximum fine-tuning epochs; unset keeps upstream's default --ribotie_patience null Early-stopping patience; unset keeps upstream's default --ribotie_checkpoint null Fine-tuned .rt.ckpt written into the config's transfer_checkpoint lines

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • --ribotie_checkpoint rewrites only transfer_checkpoint lines already in the config, all to one path and with a two-space indent; upstream's trained_model block nests that key deeper and gives each fold its own checkpoint. Check the rewritten config.yml in the work directory. The file is not staged, so it must be visible inside the container.

docs.title: Riboformer
docs.text:
Predict codon-level ribosome density in a target condition from a reference ribo-seq dataset and the coding sequence.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/lingxusb/Riboformer
  • License: MIT (code and weights)
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-riboformer-cpu and rnazoo-riboformer).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Riboformer reads the reference density and the codons in a 40-codon window and predicts the target-condition density at that codon. Upstream's data_processing.py builds the windows and transfer.py applies one of five pretrained models:

Model Predicts yeast_disome (default) Yeast disome profiles bacteria_cm_mg E. coli profiles, high-Mg flash-frozen protocol yeast_aging Aged yeast (day 4) worm_aging Aged worm (day 12) covid_model SARS-CoV-2 (24 hpi)

docs.title: Input
docs.text: A directory with the WIGs <reference>_f.wig, <reference>_r.wig, <target>_f.wig and <target>_r.wig, one genome ending in .fasta and one annotation ending in .gff3. WIG headers must keep the layout of the bundled files, fixedStep chrom=<FASTA id> start=1 step=1 with two spaces between fields, as upstream reads the name by position. Only CDSs over 200 nt in the top --riboformer_threshold percent by reference coverage are scored. The target WIGs must exist, though prediction reads only the reference. Example: tests/data/riboformer/.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In results/riboformer/: model_prediction.txt, one predicted density per window and line, on the log2 scale used in training; pause_indices.txt, copied through only if the input has one; and, with --riboformer_plot true, ribosome_density_plot.png. The gene and codon of each window (zc.txt) stay in the task work directory, under datasets/nf_input/.

Example (test profile, bacteria_cm_mg):

5.106406211853027344e+00
4.372481346130371094e+00

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
Mount the data directory into datasets/; the outputs, zc.txt included, are written into it.

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/data_dir:/opt/Riboformer/datasets/my_data \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-riboformer-cpu:latest \
  bash -c "python data_processing.py -d my_data -r ref_sample -t target_sample && python transfer.py -i my_data -m yeast_disome"

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-riboformer:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --riboformer_input /path/to/data_dir \
  --riboformer_reference_wig ref_sample \
  --riboformer_target_wig target_sample

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/riboformer/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --riboformer_input null Input directory --riboformer_reference_wig null Reference WIG name, without _f.wig (required) --riboformer_target_wig null Target WIG name (required) --riboformer_model yeast_disome Pretrained model --riboformer_psite 14 P-site offset (nt) --riboformer_wsize 40 Window in codons; the models need 40 --riboformer_threshold 25 Percent of genes kept, by reference coverage --riboformer_bundled_dataset null Dataset in the image, instead of --riboformer_input --riboformer_plot false Plot the predictions

docs.title: Bundled datasets
docs.text:
Of upstream's datasets in /opt/Riboformer/datasets/, only GSE119104_Mg_buffer (E. coli) and GSE139036_disome (yeast) have WIG, FASTA and GFF3 files. For the E. coli set:

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --riboformer_bundled_dataset GSE119104_Mg_buffer \
  --riboformer_reference_wig GSM3358138_filter_Cm_ctrl \
  --riboformer_target_wig GSM3358140_freeze_Mg_ctrl \
  --riboformer_model bacteria_cm_mg

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• transfer.py predicts every *xc.txt in the dataset folder, and each bundled dataset already holds one, so bundled runs mix precomputed windows into the output. Keep no other *xc.txt in your own input.
  • Preprocessing fails if too few genes pass the filters; use five or more, or lower --riboformer_threshold.

docs.title: SPOT-RNA
docs.text:
Predict RNA secondary structure, including pseudoknots and non-canonical base pairs.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2019
  • Upstream: https://github.com/jaswindersingh2/SPOT-RNA
  • License: MPL-2.0 (code). The model archive is hosted outside the repository and states no terms of its own; the README names MPL-2.0 for the project without saying whether it covers the archive, so commercial use and redistribution of the weights are unclear.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-spotrna-cpu and rnazoo-spotrna).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: SPOT-RNA is an ensemble of five networks (2D ResNet blocks, a 2D BiLSTM and a fully connected block; 17.5 million parameters in all), trained on 10,814 bpRNA structures and then on 120 high-resolution structures by transfer learning. It averages the five base-pair probability maps and calls pairs at 0.335 or more, keeping only the most probable partner of each base.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and T becomes U. There is no length cap; upstream quotes about 16 GB of RAM for sequences under 500 nt.

Example (tests/data/spotrna_test.fa):

>2zzm_B
GGCAGAUCUGAGCCUGGGAGCUCUCUGCC

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In spotrna_out/:

  • structures.txt: header, sequence and dot-bracket line for each sequence; pseudoknots use [] and {}
  • per sequence, named after the first word of its header (/ and : become _): the pairs in <name>.bpseq and <name>.ct, and the L × L pair probabilities (upper triangle) in <name>.prob
  • with plotting on: <name>_contact.png, a heatmap of <name>.prob

Example structures.txt, for the input above:

>2zzm_B
GGCAGAUCUGAGCCUGGGAGCUCUCUGCC
((((((...(((((...).))))))))))

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-spotrna-cpu:latest \
  spotrna_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out --cpu 4

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-spotrna:latest, add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and replace --cpu 4 with --gpu 0 (the default, --gpu -1, runs on the CPU). Add --plot for the heatmaps.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --spotrna_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. On the CPU, SPOT-RNA uses --task_cpus threads (default 4). Results go to results/spotrna/spotrna_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --spotrna_input null FASTA file --spotrna_plot false Also write <name>_contact.png heatmaps

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• If any sequence yields no structure, the run fails after the others finish and names it.
  • The dot-bracket line has three bracket levels; a pair that fits none appears only in the .bpseq and .ct files.

docs.title: Saluki
docs.text:
Predict mRNA half-life from sequence.

  • Paper: Genome Biology 2022
  • Upstream: https://github.com/calico/basenji (Saluki model)
  • License: Apache-2.0 code; CC BY 4.0 weights (Zenodo)
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-saluki-cpu and rnazoo-saluki).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Saluki is a convolutional and recurrent (GRU) network trained on consensus half-lives of 13,921 human and 14,463 mouse genes. Per nucleotide it reads A, C, G, U, a codon-frame bit (first nucleotide of each CDS codon) and a splice bit (last nucleotide of each exon). RNA-Zoo averages 50 models. The score is the first principal component of standardized log half-lives: unitless, not hours or log2 units. Higher means more stable.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA with the UTRs in lowercase and the CDS in uppercase, named by the first word of the header. The frame bits are set only if the uppercase span is a multiple of 3 nt. Transcripts over 12,288 nt keep their last 12,288 nt.

>tx1
gcgccgagcggcATGCTGTGCGGCCGCTGGTGAcgaccgtctag

Recommended: a TSV of exon lengths in transcript order, which sets the splice bits as in training. They must sum to the sequence length, or the run stops; transcripts without a row get no splice bits and are listed in a warning.

name    exon_lengths
tx1 20,24

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In results/saluki/saluki_out/, predictions.tsv holds one row per transcript: the mean and standard deviation over the 50 models, and whether exon lengths were given.

name    saluki_score_mean   saluki_score_sd splice_channel_set

preds.npy holds every model's score, shape (N, 1, 50), in the row order of names.txt.

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/exons.tsv:/data/exons.tsv \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-saluki-cpu:latest \
  saluki_predict.py -i /data/input.fa --exons /data/exons.tsv -o /out

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-saluki:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --saluki_input /path/to/input.fa --saluki_exons /path/to/exons.tsv

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/saluki/saluki_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --saluki_input null FASTA, UTRs lowercase and CDS uppercase --saluki_exons null Exon-length TSV (name, exon_lengths); recommended --saluki_species human Output head; only human works

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • --saluki_species mouse (wrapper --data-head 1) fails: the image builds the model with one output head, so loading the mouse head raises an IndexError.

docs.title: SpliceAI
docs.text:
Predict the effect of genetic variants on RNA splicing.

  • Paper: Cell 2019
  • Upstream: https://github.com/Illumina/SpliceAI
  • License: The image installs SpliceAI 1.3.1 from PyPI. At that release the source is GPL-3.0-or-later and the model weights carry no license statement. The current upstream repository is under PolyForm Strict 1.0.0 (non-commercial) and states that the weights are CC BY-NC 4.0. Commercial users should obtain a license from Illumina. The RNA-Zoo image is redistributed with the permission of the model's authors; anyone using it is bound by these terms.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-spliceai-cpu and rnazoo-spliceai).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: SpliceAI is a residual network of 32 dilated convolutions that reads 5,000 nt on each side of every scored position; five models are averaged. It scores how much a variant raises or lowers the use of nearby positions as splice acceptors and donors.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
1. A VCF of variants.
  2. A reference FASTA. A .fai index beside it is used if present; otherwise one is built in the work directory on each run.
  3. A gene annotation: grch37 (bundled GENCODE V24lift37 canonical transcripts), grch38 (bundled GENCODE V24 canonical transcripts), or a custom tab-separated file with the columns #NAME CHROM STRAND TX_START TX_END EXON_START EXON_END and exon coordinates comma-separated with a trailing comma, as in upstream's spliceai/annotations/grch37.txt.

Example (upstream examples/input.vcf, GRCh37, annotation grch37):

##fileformat=VCFv4.2
##contig=<ID=19,length=59128983>
#CHROM  POS ID  REF ALT QUAL    FILTER  INFO
19  38958362    .   C   T   .   .   .

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
spliceai_out/<input name>.spliceai.vcf: the input records, with a SpliceAI INFO entry for each scored allele and gene, ALLELE|SYMBOL|DS_AG|DS_AL|DS_DG|DS_DL|DP_AG|DP_AL|DP_DG|DP_DL. The delta scores (0 to 1) cover acceptor gain, acceptor loss, donor gain and donor loss; the delta positions place each change relative to the variant (positive is downstream). Upstream reads the largest delta score as the probability that the variant alters splicing; the paper characterizes cutoffs of 0.2 (high recall), 0.5 (recommended) and 0.8 (high precision).

Example (upstream examples/output.vcf):

19  38958362    .   C   T   .   .   SpliceAI=T|RYR1|0.00|0.00|0.91|0.08|-28|-46|-2|-31

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/inputs:/work \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-spliceai-cpu:latest \
  spliceai_predict.py -i /work/variants.vcf -o /work/variants.spliceai.vcf \
    -r /work/genome.fa -a grch38

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-spliceai:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. A custom annotation goes in /work (-a /work/annotation.tsv); -d and -m set the distance and the mask.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --spliceai_vcf /path/to/variants.vcf \
  --spliceai_reference_fasta /path/to/genome.fa \
  --spliceai_annotation grch38

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/spliceai/spliceai_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --spliceai_vcf null Input VCF --spliceai_reference_fasta null Reference FASTA; required --spliceai_annotation grch38 grch37, grch38 or the path to a custom annotation file --spliceai_distance 50 Maximum distance (0 to 4999) between the variant and a gained or lost splice site --spliceai_mask 0 1 sets gains at annotated sites and losses at unannotated sites to 0; upstream recommends 1 for variant interpretation, 0 for alternative splicing analysis

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only SNVs and simple indels (REF or ALT a single base) get scores. Other REF and ALT pairs get an entry of dots; symbolic, missing and * alleles get none.
  • Records get no SpliceAI field when the variant is outside every annotated gene, within 5 kb of a chromosome end, has a REF allele longer than twice --spliceai_distance, or does not match the reference FASTA.

docs.title: SpliceBERT
docs.text:
Extract RNA embeddings from a BERT model pretrained on vertebrate primary RNA (pre-mRNA) sequences.

  • Paper: Briefings in Bioinformatics 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/biomed-AI/SpliceBERT
  • License: BSD-3-Clause (code), CC BY 4.0 (weights, Zenodo 7995778); both allow public Docker redistribution.
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-splicebert-cpu and rnazoo-splicebert).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: SpliceBERT is a 6-layer BERT encoder (width 512, 16 attention heads, 19.4 million parameters) pretrained by masked language modeling on over 2 million primary RNA sequences, introns included, from 72 vertebrates. The image holds the SpliceBERT.1024nt checkpoint. The wrapper returns one 512-d embedding per sequence, the mean over its nucleotide positions, and optionally one per nucleotide.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA. Letters are uppercased and U becomes T, since the model was trained on DNA letters. Sequences over 1,024 nt are truncated with a warning (the model has 1,026 positions, two of them for the start and end tokens); empty sequences are skipped. Upstream warns that the model may not work on sequences shorter than 64 nt, the shortest length in its pretraining.

Example (tests/data/splicebert_test.fa, sequences shortened):

>splicebert_test_1_exon_intron_exon
CAGAGCAGACAACUAAGUGCUAUCAACUAGGC...
>splicebert_test_4_short
GCAACACACCGUAUCGGUCCUAGGAGGUCUGC...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In splicebert_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, 512), one row per sequence
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (L, 512), for each sequence (spaces and / in the header become _)

Example, for the four sequences in tests/data/splicebert_test.fa:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("splicebert_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (4, 512)
names = open("splicebert_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # ['splicebert_test_1_exon_intron_exon', ...]

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-splicebert-cpu:latest \
  splicebert_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-splicebert:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Add --per-token for per-nucleotide embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --splicebert_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/splicebert/splicebert_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --splicebert_input null FASTA file --splicebert_per_token false Also write per-nucleotide embeddings --splicebert_max_len 1024 Truncate longer sequences to this many nt --splicebert_batch_size 8 Sequences per forward pass; lower it if GPU memory runs out

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Pretraining used vertebrate sequences only.
  • Only embeddings are exposed: upstream's splice-site and branchpoint prediction examples are not wired in, and RNA-Zoo has no fine-tuning flags for SpliceBERT.
  • A warning at load time that the pooler weights are newly initialized is expected; the wrapper does not use the pooler.

docs.title: TranslationAI
docs.text:
Predict translation initiation sites (TIS), translation termination sites (TTS), and ORFs from mRNA sequence.

  • Paper: NAR 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/rnasys/TranslationAI
  • License: AGPL-3.0 (source code) + CC BY-NC 4.0 (model weights, non-commercial only)
  • Device: CPU. The pipeline runs rnazoo-translationai-cpu under both profiles, because TranslationAI's command-line entry point hides every GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: A 32-layer dilated residual CNN, trained on human RefSeq protein-coding transcripts, scores every mRNA position as a TIS or TTS (five models with 2,000 nt of context, averaged) and pairs in-frame TIS and TTS calls into ORFs. Length is not capped.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA with A, C, G, T or N only, each sequence on one line, and headers in upstream's layout >chrN:start-end(strand)(name)(TIS, TTS,); other headers stop the run.

>chr3:28283123-28361264(+)(CMC1)(241, 568,)
GAGGGAACGGGTCCTGGCGGTGCTTTGCAAAGGG...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In results/translationai/, named after the input and the thresholds: <input>_predTIS_<t>.txt and <input>_predTTS_<t>.txt (the header, then position,score per site, best first), and <input>_predORFs_<t>_<t>.txt (the header, then TIS,TTS,TIS_score,TTS_score per pair, best product first; transcripts without a pair are left out). Positions are 0-based and mark the first base of the start or stop codon.

Example (translationai_test_predTIS_0.5.txt from the test profile):

>chr3:28283123-28361264(+)(CMC1)(241, 568,) 241,0.8824475854635239

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
TranslationAI writes next to its input, so the command works on a copy in /tmp:

docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-translationai-cpu:latest \
  bash -c "cp /data/input.fa /tmp/input.fa && translationai -I /tmp/input.fa -t 0.5,0.5 && cp /tmp/input_pred*.txt /out/"

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --translationai_input /path/to/input.fa

-profile docker,gpu runs the same CPU image. Results go to results/translationai/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --translationai_input null FASTA file --translationai_tis_threshold 0.5 Below 1, the minimum TIS score; 1 or more, the number of top TIS per transcript --translationai_tts_threshold 0.5 The same for TTS

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • An ORF pairs any predicted TIS with any predicted TTS downstream in the same frame, without checking for stop codons in between.

docs.title: UTR-LM
docs.text:
Predict mean ribosome loading, translation efficiency or expression level from 5' UTR sequences.

  • Paper: Nature Machine Intelligence 2024
  • Upstream: https://github.com/a96123155/UTR-LM
  • License: GPL-3.0
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-utrlm-cpu and rnazoo-utrlm).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
UTR-LM is a 6-layer transformer (1.2 million parameters with the MRL head) pretrained on 5' UTRs, including 214,349 Ensembl 5' UTRs from human, rat, mouse, chicken and zebrafish. A small head reads the embedding of the start token:

Task Predicts Scored part of each UTR Head trained on mrl Mean ribosome loading Last 50 nt Synthetic 50-nt 5' UTR libraries te Log translation efficiency (Ribo-seq over RNA-seq RPKM) Last 100 nt HEK293T, PC3 or human muscle (--utrlm_cell_line) el Log expression level (RNA-seq RPKM) Last 100 nt Same three

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA of 5' UTRs; U becomes T. Only the last 50 nt (mrl) or 100 nt (te, el) of each sequence are scored; shorter sequences are scored whole.

Example (from tests/data/utrlm_test.fa):

>synthetic_utr_1
AATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAA
>synthetic_utr_3
ATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATG

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
utrlm_out/predictions.tsv: header, sequence (the scored part) and one prediction column, mean_ribosome_loading, translation_efficiency_log or expression_level_log.

Example, mrl task (the 51-nt synthetic_utr_3 loses its first base):

header  sequence    mean_ribosome_loading
synthetic_utr_1 AATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAATTCCGGAA  8.053340
synthetic_utr_3 TGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATGATG  6.575327

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-utrlm-cpu:latest \
  utrlm_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out --task mrl --model-dir /opt/utrlm/Model

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-utrlm:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. For te or el, add --cell-line HEK, pc3 or Muscle. Prediction uses cross-validation fold 0; --folds all averages the 10 folds of te and el (mrl ships fold 0 only).

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --utrlm_input /path/to/input.fa --utrlm_task mrl

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/utrlm/utrlm_out/.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description --utrlm_input null FASTA of 5' UTRs --utrlm_task mrl mrl, te or el --utrlm_cell_line HEK HEK, pc3 or Muscle; used by te and el --utrlm_checkpoint null Absolute path to a fine-tuned .pt, used instead of the bundled weights

docs.title: Fine-tuning on your own data
docs.text:
Trains the backbone and head on a table with a utr column and a numeric label column (read as tab-separated only if the file name ends in .tsv, otherwise as CSV):

nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu \
  --utrlm_finetune_input my_training_data.csv \
  --utrlm_finetune_label my_mrl \
  --utrlm_finetune_task mrl

The weights with the lowest validation loss are kept. Outputs in results/utrlm_finetune/utrlm_finetune_out/: best_model.pt and predictions.tsv (the input table plus a predicted column, for all rows). To predict with the checkpoint, pass its absolute path as --utrlm_checkpoint with the same --utrlm_task.

Parameter Default Description --utrlm_finetune_input null Training table --utrlm_finetune_label null (required) Label column --utrlm_finetune_task mrl mrl, te or el; sets the backbone variant and scored length --utrlm_finetune_epochs 100 Maximum epochs --utrlm_finetune_patience 20 Early-stopping patience (epochs) --utrlm_finetune_lr 0.01 Adam learning rate --utrlm_finetune_batch_size 32 Batch size --utrlm_finetune_val_frac 0.2 Fraction of rows held out for validation --utrlm_finetune_pretrained null Checkpoint to start from; without it, training starts from random weights

Known issue: fine-tuning fails at the first batch (ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 2)): bin/utrlm_finetune.py gives UTR-LM's batch converter two fields per sequence instead of four. The head trainer on foundation-model embeddings is an alternative.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • For el with Muscle, two checkpoints match each fold; the wrapper takes whichever the file system lists first.

docs.title: mRNABERT
docs.text:
Extract embeddings of mRNAs, with one token per UTR nucleotide and one per CDS codon.

  • Paper: Nature Communications 2025
  • Upstream: https://github.com/yyly6/mRNABERT; weights and model code: Hugging Face YYLY66/mRNABERT
  • License: Apache-2.0 (code and weights, per the Hugging Face model card)
  • Device: CPU or GPU (images rnazoo-mrnabert-cpu and rnazoo-mrnabert).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: mRNABERT is a 12-layer BERT-style encoder (width 768, 113.4 million parameters) that uses ALiBi attention biases instead of position embeddings. It was pretrained by masked language modeling on about 18 million mRNA sequences, then aligned with protein embeddings by contrastive learning on 500,000 CDS and protein pairs. The wrapper returns one 768-d embedding per sequence, the mean over its tokens, and optionally one per token.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
FASTA of mRNA sequences, with T or U. The wrapper uppercases them, turns U into T and picks the CDS itself: the longest ORF that runs from an ATG to the first in-frame stop codon. The ORF is tokenized as codons and the rest as single nucleotides; a sequence without an ORF is read as all UTR. The wrapper logs the ORF it picked for each sequence. Sequences over 1,022 tokens (1,024 with [CLS] and [SEP]) are truncated with a warning; empty sequences are skipped.

Example (tests/data/rnafm_test.fa, used by the test profile; sequences shortened; only test_rna_2 has an ORF):

>test_rna_1
GGGUGCGAUCAUACCAGCACUAAUGCCCUCCUGG...
>test_rna_2
AUUCCGAGAGCUAACGGAGAACUCUGUUCGAUUU...

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
In mrnabert_out/:

  • sequence_embeddings.npy: shape (N, 768), one row per sequence ([CLS] and [SEP] excluded from the mean)
  • labels.txt: the FASTA headers, in row order
  • with per-token output: <header>_tokens.npy, shape (T, 768) for T tokens, including [CLS] (first row) and [SEP] (last row). Spaces and / in the header become _.

The model card's example averages over all tokens, [CLS] and [SEP] included; pool the per-token output to match it.

Example, for the input above:

import numpy as np
emb = np.load("mrnabert_out/sequence_embeddings.npy")       # shape (2, 768)
names = open("mrnabert_out/labels.txt").read().splitlines()  # ['test_rna_1', 'test_rna_2']

docs.title: Run with Docker
docs.text:
docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -e USER=$(whoami) \
  -v /path/to/input.fa:/data/input.fa \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/ericmalekos/rnazoo-mrnabert-cpu:latest \
  mrnabert_predict.py -i /data/input.fa -o /out

For the GPU image, use rnazoo-mrnabert:latest and add --runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Add --per-token for per-token embeddings.

docs.title: Run with Nextflow
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile docker,cpu --mrnabert_input /path/to/input.fa

Use -profile docker,gpu for the GPU image. Results go to results/mrnabert/mrnabert_out/.

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: Train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on frozen mRNABERT embeddings, as the Fine Tuning guide describes. Its common parameters take the prefix mrnabert: --mrnabert_finetune_input and --mrnabert_finetune_label are required, and --mrnabert_finetune_embeddings reuses saved embeddings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The CDS is chosen by ORF length alone, and CDS coordinates cannot be supplied: a longer spurious ORF wins over the true CDS.
  • Both images use plain PyTorch attention: the GPU image disables upstream's Triton kernel, which does not compile there. Warnings at load about Triton and the uninitialized pooler are expected; the wrapper does not use the pooler.

docs.title: Model Overview
docs.text: RNA-Zoo runs 23 models in six tracks: 13 task programs and 10 embedding models. Each model runs in its own container image, with its weights inside.

docs.title: Translation
docs.text: RiboNN, TranslationAI, Saluki and CodonTransformer need only sequences. Riboformer and RiboTIE also need ribosome profiling data: Riboformer predicts the density in a target condition from a reference dataset, and RiboTIE fine-tunes on each sample's reads before it calls ORFs.

docs.title: RNA foundation models
docs.text:
The nine foundation models and SpliceBERT (splicing track) return embeddings: one vector per sequence in sequence_embeddings.npy, the names in labels.txt, and one vector per token with --<model>_per_token. They differ in size, pretraining data and input limit:

Model Parameters Width Pretraining data Max input RNA-FM 99.5M 640 23M non-coding RNAs (RNAcentral) 1,022 nt RiNALMo 650.9M 1280 36M non-coding RNAs (RNAcentral and other databases) No cap; memory-bound ERNIE-RNA 86.3M 768 20.4M non-coding RNAs (RNAcentral) 1,022 nt Orthrus 10.2M (default checkpoint) 512 (256 for two checkpoints) Splice isoforms of ten metazoans and orthologs from over 400 mammals, by contrastive learning No cap HydraRNA 84.2M 1024 28M non-coding RNAs and mRNAs No cap; 10,240-nt chunks, averaged RNAErnie 86.6M 768 About 31M RNAcentral sequences (a later PyTorch model by the authors, not the paper's) 2,046 nt PlantRNA-FM 33.8M 480 Transcripts of 1,124 plant species (about 25M sequences) 1,024 nt CaLM 85.7M 768 9M coding sequences (European Nucleotide Archive) 1,024 codons mRNABERT 113.4M 768 About 18M mRNAs 1,022 tokens (UTR nucleotides and CDS codons) SpliceBERT 19.4M 512 Over 2M primary RNAs from 72 vertebrates 1,024 nt

Inputs over the limit are truncated with a warning. The sequence embedding is the mean over positions, without the start and end tokens; ERNIE-RNA instead returns its CLS token.

docs.title: RNA structure
docs.text: RhoFold and DRfold2 predict 3D structure from a single sequence. RhoFold takes up to 1,022 nt and runs on CPU or GPU; DRfold2 has no length cap but needs a GPU. SPOT-RNA predicts secondary structure, including pseudoknots and non-canonical pairs.

docs.title: Splicing
docs.text: SpliceAI and Pangolin score variants against a reference genome and a gene annotation. SpliceBERT only returns embeddings.

docs.title: Fine-tuning
docs.text: The nine foundation models can train a linear, MLP or XGBoost head on their frozen embeddings and your labels; see the Fine Tuning guide. SpliceBERT has no fine-tuning parameters. RiboTIE fine-tunes its pretrained models on each sample's reads in every run. RiboNN and UTR-LM have their own fine-tuning modules, but both currently fail and are not tested; a fix is planned for a later release.
